newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds weaker on soft dollar, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds weaker on soft dollar, profit-taking.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Tuesday as a weak Canadian dollar and broad-based profit-taking combined to drive down the prices of Canada's benchmark 30-year and 10-year bonds, analysts said.
The weakness came on the heels of a bond market rally on Monday, when bullish trading pushed the yield on Canada's 30-year bond to a record low.

"This was an overdue correction, but not a major one in light of the gains of the last week. We've only lost a third of a point at the long end," said Andrew Pyle, vice-president of fixed-income research with ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett.
Canada's benchmark 30-year long bond fell C$0.52 to C$118 to yield 6.606 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond dipped 5/32 to yield 6.59 percent. The spread between the bonds moved to a negative spread of one basis point, the same as Monday's close.
The Canadian 30-year long bond hit a record low on Monday as North American bond prices continued to rally on speculation that the U.S. economy had reached near-perfect market conditions.
Canadian bonds have rallied in the past week since the U.S. Federal Reserve decided not to raise interest rates.
But a soft Canadian dollar brought the bond rally to a premature end in early morning trading.
The dollar opened weaker at C$1.3792 (US$0.7250) before staging a modest comeback to close at C$1.3735 (US$0.7280).
Pyle said the failure of the Canadian dollar to strengthen past C$1.3710 (US$0.7293) gave the bond market a compelling reason not to keep extending positions.

Analysts said new supply also heightened the downward trend in bond markets. The Government of Quebec set a C$350 million 6.5 percent bond due October 1, 2007, said lead manager Levesque Beaubien Geoffrion on Tuesday.
The bond was priced at 100.871 to yield 6.381 percent, 36 basis points over the Government of Canada 7.25 percent bond due June, 2007.
"There were a few new issues focused in the 10-year area that added some supply pressure," said a trader at a Canadian-based brokerage.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.28 to C$109.12 to yield 6.010 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent, which lost 1/32 to yield 6.26 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 25 basis points from 28 basis points at the close of trading on Monday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.06 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 4.97 percent.
